note: Line key = id + lang. fr-CA and en-CA entries share the same id stem. Classes: a fixed UI and Numa, b feedback, c number/unit/operator vocabulary, d world and chapter intros, e question prompts (generated from seed/questions), f canned story beats. Priorities P1..P6: record in order. No em dashes in kid-facing text.

speaker.reader: Same actor, plainer reading voice for prompts and number words

voiceDirection.fr-CA: Numa est une chouette chaleureuse, curieuse et douce, avec une pointe de jeu. Voix naturelle de Québécoise ou Québécois, sourire audible, débit tranquille, comme on parle à un enfant de 6 à 9 ans que l’on aime bien. Jamais de déception, jamais de soupir, jamais de pression : une réponse fausse est un détour, pas un échec. Accent québécois naturel, sans exagération. Ne dis pas les mots entre crochets. Reste la même personne d’une séance à l’autre : même micro, même distance, même énergie.
voiceDirection.en-CA: Numa is a warm, curious, kind owl with a little playfulness. Natural Canadian English, smile audible in the voice, relaxed pace, as if talking to a child of 6 to 9 you like. Never disappointed, never a sigh, never pressure: a wrong answer is a detour, not a failure. Keep the same person across sessions: same mic, same distance, same energy.

directionCodes.B: bright, genuinely pleased, smile in the voice, never shouty
directionCodes.G: gentle, encouraging, never disappointed, no sigh, no drop in energy
directionCodes.Q: curious, a little playful, wonder rising on the key word
directionCodes.H: calm and helpful, like leaning in to share a tip
directionCodes.P: clear, friendly, steady pace for a 6 to 8 year old, no pressure; lift only on the final question
directionCodes.N: even and clear, medium pitch, no emphasis, flat-neutral so it joins other clips

fr-CA.rules: 0-16 words; 17-19 dix-sept..dix-neuf; 20-69 tens + "et un" at 21/31/41/51/61 else hyphen; 70 soixante-dix, 71 soixante et onze, 72-79 soixante-douze..; 80 quatre-vingts (final, no s when followed by a number); 81-99 quatre-vingt-un..quatre-vingt-dix-neuf (no "et"); 100 cent; cents when final and multiplied (deux cents) else cent; mille invariable; Belgian/Swiss septante, octante, nonante are NOT used in Quebec

en-CA.rules: 0-19 words; tens hyphenated (twenty-one); hundred; "and" optional after hundred, use none in maths speech ("one hundred twenty"); thousand; million; decimals say "point" then digits
